turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, doctor. Siyabonga's here, twenty one, mom came with. Shame, my sister in Gqeberha was up all night with her little one, cough and all, so I'm a bit raw myself.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, sister. Siyabonga, howzit. What's brought you in?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Bones.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His legs and his back, doctor. He's been holding them and...
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long's that been going?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Two days.
[SEG0007] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja. The exact start though, uh, Saturday after the braai or Sunday, I can't...
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): You can't pin the hour. Alright, we'll call it two days. Any fever with it?
[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A bit. Mild.
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Hot.
[SEG0011] person_1 (NURSE): Obs are done. Blood pressure one eighteen over seventy two, pulse 98, temp 37.8, sats 97, breathing 18.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Mild temp. Chest pain?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Short of breath?
[SEG0015] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He doesn't like those masks, he gets...
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Tummy, waterworks, any of that playing up?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): The sickle cell, that's known, ne. Crises before?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0021] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Since he was small. The last bad one was last winter, or the one before, umm, I really don't know which.
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Dunno.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): So we can't date that last one. Err, still on the folic acid?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): What dose?
[SEG0026] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ag, the card is in the other bag, I think I left it in the...
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Five.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, five milligrams, every morning.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the hydroxyurea, you're taking that?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The hydroxurea. Five hundred milligrams, one capsule at night.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Every night. Any reactions to medicines? Rash, swelling, anything?
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Maybe.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Maybe what happened?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Rash.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which drug was it?
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): Dunno.
[SEG0038] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): They said maybe the penicillin or the septrin. Nobody told us which one did the rash.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok. So we're not sure of the culprit. I won't touch penicillin or septrin today. Let me have a look.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Eish. Both shins are tender when I press, and the lower back too. Chest is clear. Slight yellow tinge in the eyes. Throat is fine.

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking this is a mild vaso-occlusive episode. The red cells stiffen and block the little vessels in the bone, so the bone hurts because the blood can't get through properly. Fever's low, but I can't exclude a brewing infection until the bloods are back.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Ok.
[SEG0043] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is it dangerous? Because last time he...
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not looking severe, mom. We'll treat the pain and check the blood. I'm sending bloods now, full blood count, urea and electrolytes, and a retic count.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): I'll take him through just now for those.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Paracetamol, one gram every six hours, by mouth. Push fluids, two to three litres today, and rest the legs.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0048] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not the strong one? He was on...
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not yet. If the pain is still bad this evening we can add something else, but not now. Come back in two days so I can see the results and the pain.
[SEG0050] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Friday, or...
[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): In two days, ja. And if the pain gets worse or you can't keep fluids down, come back sooner, even tonight.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Ok.
[SEG0053] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thank you, doctor. We'll do the water, hey.
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sharp. Sister's got the bloods. Go well.

spec.situation: Young adult with known sickle cell disease and bone pains for two days, fever mild; takes folic acid and hydroxyurea; fluids and painkiller plan; blood tests planned.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

omissions.text: Past history of prior sickle cell crises since childhood was explicitly confirmed ('Crises before?' 'Ja.' / 'Since he was small'), whereas the recorded past crisis is incorrectly represented as a resolved crisis with onset 'last winter or the one before' rather than recurrent prior crises with uncertain date of the last severe episode.
Doctor stated he would avoid penicillin and septrin today because of the uncertain prior rash history ('I won't touch penicillin or septrin today').
Doctor advised that if pain is still bad this evening, additional analgesia could be added later, but not now.
Follow-up in two days was specifically to review both the blood results and the pain.
